Non-high-poverty (<20%) block groups: Island and Fringe CIs remain above IRR = 1.0 (Fig. 8b), whereas Outlying without high poverty has IRR = 0.91 and is "not found to be significantly associated with unsewered areas" (PDF pp. 7-8, Fig. 8b; N = 31,383; Model 6 of Supplementary Table 6).

Highest poverty tercile (>=20.5% poverty) median % unsewered: Islands = 19.0%, Outlying = 11.8%, Fringe = 4.5%, Incorporated = 0%.

headline_result_summary: Across 31,383 U.S. Census block groups in nine states, unincorporated status (vs. municipal incorporation as the referent) is significantly associated with worse centralized wastewater and drinking water coverage—modeled as a higher relative risk (incidence rate ratio, IRR > 1; positive raw regression sign) of block group community land area being UNSERVED. In multilevel negative binomial regressions with county and state random effects, unincorporated status among high-poverty block groups (>=20% poverty) is associated with 3.54 times greater unsewered land area and 17.8 times greater land area unserved by centralized water; among non-high-poverty block groups, unincorporated status is associated with 1.48 times greater unsewered area. Disaggregating unincorporated communities into Island, Fringe, and Outlying types shows that sewer deficits are sharpest in unincorporated Islands near municipal boundaries (IRR = 2.47 without poverty interaction; IRR > 4.0 in high-poverty Islands and Outlying areas, though null [IRR = 0.91] in non-high-poverty Outlying areas), whereas centralized drinking water deficits are sharpest in Outlying and high-poverty Fringe communities (IRR = 5.53 for Outlying without poverty interaction). Substantively, unincorporated status / municipal exclusion is unfavorable to household access (equivalently, municipal incorporation is favorable to household access).
specification_or_coding_pitfalls: 1. DOUBLE SIGN / POLARITY TRAP (Crucial): (a) Outcome polarity is inverted relative to coverage: the regression dependent variable is block group land area NOT served (unsewered / unserved rate Y_ij / A_ij), NOT percent covered. Consequently, a positive regression coefficient (beta > 0, IRR > 1.0, raw_sign = 'positive') means MORE unserved area = LOWER coverage = WORSE access. (b) Exposure pole orientation: in all regressions, 'Incorporated' is the referent category (= 0) and 'Unincorporated' (or Island/Fringe/Outlying) is the coded exposure (= 1). Under the authors' coding (Unincorporated vs. Incorporated), the substantive effect is 'unfavorable_to_access'. However, if a review synthesis defines the legal/governance intervention positively as 'municipal incorporation / legal inclusion' (Incorporated vs. Unincorporated), the exact same empirical result flips to 'favorable_to_access' (incorporated municipalities have higher sewer and water coverage). 2. SUPPLEMENTARY TABLES: All 13 numeric tables (including full regression outputs in Supplementary Tables 5 and 6) are hosted in online Supplementary Information rather than printed in the 17-page main article PDF; the main text reports exact IRRs, sample sizes, means/medians, and Figure 8 forest plots with 95% CIs, but exact SEs and p-values are in the supplement. 3. SUBGROUP HETEROGENEITY: While unincorporated status overall is strongly associated with unserved area, Outlying unincorporated block groups WITHOUT high poverty (<20%) have IRR = 0.91 and are not significantly associated with unsewered area (PDF p. 8), and Island communities do not show a significantly greater high-poverty penalty than incorporated communities for centralized drinking water (PDF p. 8). 4. SPATIAL ECOLOGICAL COVERAGE METRIC: Coverage is measured spatially as the proportion of settled 'community' land area (>250 parcels/sq mi) within utility service area boundaries (or residential parcels in Florida), rather than household-level survey connection or affordability/tariff data.
study_design: Cross-sectional observational spatial/ecological study using multilevel Negative Binomial Generalized Linear Models (GLM) with county-level and state-level random intercepts and a log block group land area offset, controlling for high poverty (and unincorporated x high-poverty interactions), population density, and percent rural population.
unit_and_sample_size: 31,383 U.S. Census block groups (2010 Census boundaries; 2008-2012 5-year ACS poverty estimates) containing settled 'community' land (>250 parcels per square mile) across 9 states representing >25% of the U.S. population (83% incorporated block groups; ~6% Island, ~8% Fringe, and 2.7% [n = 845] Outlying unincorporated block groups; average population 1,538 per block group; >10 million people residing in unincorporated communities; utility data covering 5,220 POTW plus 9,087,949 residential parcels in Florida and 10,948 community water systems).
